body.name: Total pilot-split certified QTE radius
body.construction:
For each cell, assign the first \(r_{n,\ell}=\lceil n_\ell^{3/4}\rceil\) pre observations and the first \(r_{m,\ell}=\lceil m_\ell^{3/4}\rceil\) post observations to a pilot, with the original observation order breaking all ties; use the remaining \(N_{n,\ell}=n_\ell-r_{n,\ell}\) and \(N_{m,\ell}=m_\ell-r_{m,\ell}\) observations for a main-sample QTE center \(\widetilde\tau_{t,\ell}\).  Put \(\beta_\ell=(n_\ell\wedge m_\ell)^{-2}\) and \(\zeta_\ell=1/\log(e+n_\ell\wedge m_\ell)\).  Construct the simultaneous pilot random closed set \(\widehat{\mathcal K}_\ell\) by the binomial, DKW, density-difference, Gram, covariance, support-cluster, covariance-rank, and simplex-face intervals in \(\mathrm{lem:pilot\mbox{-}geometry\mbox{-}gaussian\mbox{-}transfer}\).  Every unresolved root-\(m_\ell\) cross-cell translation and root-\(n_\ell\) face offset is retained; only the pilot-consistent within-cell offset differences are conditioned upon.  Choose certified Gaussian tail bounds \(G,R\), compute the transfer cushion \(\delta_\ell\) from equation~(22) of that lemma, and use exhaustive rational interval arithmetic over \(\widehat{\mathcal K}_\ell\cap\Gamma_\eta^{G,R}\) to return the upper endpoint \(\overline c_\ell\) of a cutoff bracket of width at most \(\zeta_\ell\).  Let \(a^M_\ell=N_{n,\ell}^{-1}+N_{m,\ell}^{-1/2}\), let \(T^\circ_\ell=\max_{t>T_0}\|\widetilde\tau_{t,\ell}-\widehat\tau_{t,\ell}\|_{L^2}\), and on successful certification set
\[
 R_\ell=\min\{2D,\sqrt{a^M_\ell(\overline c_\ell+\delta_\ell)}+T^\circ_\ell\}.
\]
Take \(W_\ell\) to be one plus the deterministic grid-complexity bound in \(\mathrm{lem:pilot\mbox{-}geometry\mbox{-}gaussian\mbox{-}transfer}\).  If a main block is empty, a primitive region fails its deterministic checks, or certification has not succeeded by \(W_\ell\) operations, set \(R_\ell=R^{\mathrm{DKW}}_\ell\).  All enumerations use the fixed lexicographic ordering and the first certified rational bracket, so this defines one total Borel function of the data.
